# Overview

This in-class exercise follows Lesson 7. It models how easily the 3,125 hexagons covering Singapore can reach eldercare centres, using the **catchment** package to compute four floating catchment area measures. The **accessibility** package is loaded as in the lesson notes, and the tidied OD matrix below is kept in the long format it expects.

# Getting Started

## Installing the catchment package from GitHub

**catchment** is not on CRAN, so it is installed from GitHub. This only needs to run once, so the chunk is not run when the page renders.

```{r}
#| eval: false
remotes::install_github('uva-bi-sdad/catchment')
```

## Loading the packages

**here** builds file paths from the project root, so the same path works in the Console and during `quarto render`.

```{r}
#| output: false
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility, catchment, here)
```

# Importing the Data

This exercise reuses the four datasets from [Hands-on Exercise 07](../../Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex07/Hands-on_Ex07.qmd), so I read them from that folder instead of keeping a second copy.

## Importing geospatial data

The three geospatial layers are MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL, hexagons and ELDERCARE.

```{r}
#| output: false
mpsz <- st_read(dsn = here("Hands-on_Ex", "Hands-on_Ex07", "data", "geospatial"),
                layer = "MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
#| output: false
hexagons <- st_read(dsn = here("Hands-on_Ex", "Hands-on_Ex07", "data", "geospatial"),
                    layer = "hexagons") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
#| output: false
eldercare <- st_read(dsn = here("Hands-on_Ex", "Hands-on_Ex07", "data", "geospatial"),
                     layer = "ELDERCARE") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

## Importing the OD matrix

```{r}
ODMatrix <- read_csv(here("Hands-on_Ex", "Hands-on_Ex07", "data", "aspatial", "OD_Matrix.csv"),
                     skip = 0)
```

# Data Wrangling

## Supply

Each eldercare centre gets a capacity of 100, and `fid` is renamed to `id`.

```{r}
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100) %>%
  rename(id = fid)
```

## Demand

The code chunk below creates a new field called `demand` and populates it with the value 100.

```{r}
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100) %>%
  rename(id = fid)
```

## Tidying the OD matrix

The code chunk below selects `origin_id`, `destination_id` and `total_cost` from the OD matrix, then renames them to `from_id`, `to_id` and `dist`.

```{r}
ODMatrix_tidied <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  rename(from_id = origin_id,
         to_id = destination_id,
         dist = total_cost)
```

## Converting the ODMatrix data frame into a matrix

In the code chunk below, `as.matrix()` is used to convert the ODMatrix data frame into a matrix object.

```{r}
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost)%>%
  select(c(-c('origin_id')))

distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat/1000)
```

# Computing 2SFCA with the catchment Package

In the code chunk below, [`catchment_ratio()`](https://uva-bi-sdad.github.io/catchment/reference/catchment_ratio.html) is used to compute 2SFCA.

```{r}
df_2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  max_cost = 5) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping 2SFCA

The slide shows only the map, and the prof said the code comes from the hands-on exercise. `bind_cols()` attaches the 2SFCA values to the hexagons, and `st_bbox()` sets the map frame. I reuse the `acc_map()` function from my Hands-on Exercise 7.

```{r}
hexagon_2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_2sfca)
mapex <- st_bbox(hexagons)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
fmt_num <- function(v) {
  sapply(v, function(z) {
    if (z == 0) "0"
    else if (abs(z) < 0.01 || abs(z) >= 1000) formatC(z, format = "e", digits = 1)
    else if (abs(z) >= 100) format(round(z))
    else formatC(signif(z, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2)
  }) %>% trimws()
}

acc_map <- function(data, var, title, legend_title, zero_label = NULL) {
  x <- data[[var]]
  if (is.null(zero_label)) {
    q <- quantile(x, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 11))
    breaks <- c(q[1:10], Inf)
    labels <- paste(fmt_num(q[1:10]), "to", fmt_num(q[2:11]))
    fills <- "brewer.blues"
  } else {
    q <- quantile(x[x > 0], probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10))
    breaks <- c(0, q[1:9], Inf)
    labels <- c(zero_label, paste(fmt_num(q[1:9]), "to", fmt_num(q[2:10])))
    fills <- c("grey75", RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Blues"))
  }
  tm_shape(data, bbox = mapex) +
    tm_polygons(fill = var,
                fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(breaks = unname(breaks),
                                                labels = labels,
                                                values = fills),
                fill.legend = tm_legend(title = legend_title,
                                        position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
                col = "grey85", lwd = 0.2) +
  tm_shape(eldercare) +
    tm_dots(size = 0.3, fill = "#D55E00", col = "black") +
    tm_title(title, size = 1.5, fontface = "bold") +
    tm_compass(type = "8star", size = 2,
               position = c("left", "top")) +
    tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"))
}

acc_map(hexagon_2SFCA, "2SFCA",
        "2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
`r format(sum(hexagon_2SFCA$"2SFCA" == 0), big.mark = ",")` of the `r format(nrow(hexagon_2SFCA), big.mark = ",")` hexagons have a 2SFCA of 0, because no eldercare centre is within 5 km of them by road. With plain quantile classes, the lowest classes all run from 0 to 0, which is why the legend on the prof's map repeats "0.000 - -0.001". So I give the zeros their own grey class and split the rest into nine classes, pale for low and dark for high, following the colour guides from ISSS608 Lesson 2.
:::

# Computing E2SFCA with the catchment Package

## Enhanced 2-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA)

E2SFCA gives nearer centres more weight. `step_weights` sets the weight for each distance band, from 0.01 for centres between 4 and 5 km away to 1 for centres within 1 km.

```{r}
step_weights <- list(c(5, .01), c(4, .05), c(3, .1), c(2, .4), c(1, 1))
df_e2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = step_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("E2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping E2SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_E2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_e2sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
acc_map(hexagon_E2SFCA, "E2SFCA",
        "E2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "E2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```

## The Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
acc_map(hexagon_E2SFCA, "E2SFCA",
        "E2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "E2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
2SFCA counts every centre within 5 km fully, while E2SFCA cuts a centre 4 to 5 km away down to 1 percent of its weight. The two measures rank the hexagons with a Spearman correlation of `r sprintf("%.3f", cor(df_2sfca$"2SFCA", df_e2sfca$"E2SFCA", method = "spearman"))`, and E2SFCA has `r format(sum(hexagon_E2SFCA$"E2SFCA" == 0), big.mark = ",")` hexagons at 0. The steps act like a stepped version of the distance decay used in KD2SFCA in Hands-on Exercise 7.
:::

# Computing KD2SFCA with the catchment Package

## Kernel Density (Gaussian) 2-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_kd2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = "gaussian") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("KD2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping KD2SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_KD2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_kd2sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
acc_map(hexagon_KD2SFCA, "KD2SFCA",
        "KD2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "KD2SFCA")
```

## The Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
acc_map(hexagon_KD2SFCA, "KD2SFCA",
        "KD2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "KD2SFCA")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
`weight = "gaussian"` uses the weight exp(−d² / 8), because `catchment_weight()` sets the scale to 2 km unless told otherwise. There is no `max_cost` here, so no centre is ever cut off, and `r format(sum(hexagon_KD2SFCA$"KD2SFCA" == 0), big.mark = ",")` hexagons are exactly 0. That is why this map needs no grey class. A centre 2 km away still counts for about 61 percent, while one 6 km away counts for about 1 percent, so the far west only gets a tiny value.
:::

# Computing 3SFCA with the catchment Package

## 3-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_3sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  step_weights,
  normalize_weight = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("3SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping 3SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_3SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_3sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10

acc_map(hexagon_3SFCA, "3SFCA",
        "3SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "3SFCA",

```
